quests.instruction: The sign on the shop door says PUSH, but Ana pushes and nothing happens. She tries the other action. She has to…
quests.hint: What do you do to a drawer handle to open it?
quests.explanation: Pushing moves something away from you. Pulling brings it toward you. The door only opens one way.
quests.funFact: Doors that confuse people are sometimes called “Norman doors”, after a designer who wrote about everyday design.

quests.instruction: Aunt Leela holds out a tray of mangoes. Each child ___ one and says thank you.
quests.hint: Picture someone holding out a tray: whose hand reaches in?
quests.explanation: Giving means handing something to another person. Taking is what the other person does when they accept it.
quests.funFact: In Hindi, “dena” means to give and “lena” means to take.

quests.instruction: The class waited outside the library until the bell. When the library closed, everyone had to…
quests.hint: Where do you go when the librarian says it’s closing time?
quests.explanation: To enter is to go into a place. To leave is to go out of it.
quests.funFact: Revolving doors let people go in and out without letting much hot or cold air through.

quests.instruction: The train from Delhi arrives at 5:10. It pulls away again at 5:20, so the board says it…
quests.hint: Which column of the station board shows when trains pull away?
quests.explanation: Arriving means reaching a place. Departing means setting off from it.
quests.funFact: Airports and stations use “arrivals” and “departures” boards for exactly this reason.

quests.instruction: Which word is the opposite of “start”? (runners crouched at the line vs. runners breaking the ribbon at the far end)
quests.hint: Imagine the ribbon snapping at the end of a race.
quests.explanation: To start is to begin something. To finish is to reach the end of it.
quests.funFact: A marathon is 42.195 kilometres long.

quests.instruction: Hot-air balloons rise when the air inside is heated. When the burner is switched off for long enough, they slowly…
quests.hint: Which way does a balloon go once the warm air cools?
quests.explanation: Rising means moving upward. Falling means moving downward.
quests.funFact: Hot air is lighter than the cooler air around it, which is why it rises.

quests.instruction: Grandma can recite every nursery rhyme from when she was little, but she has ___ where she left her glasses.
quests.hint: Which word means a memory has slipped away?
quests.explanation: To remember is to keep something in your mind. To forget is to lose it from your mind.
quests.funFact: Repeating something a few times, or writing it down, helps your brain hold on to it.

quests.instruction: Kiran spent an hour building a sandcastle. Then a big wave rolled in and ___ it.
quests.hint: Waves don’t care how long a sandcastle took to build.
quests.explanation: Building puts something together piece by piece. Destroying wrecks it, often much faster.
quests.funFact: Sandcastles hold together best when the sand is damp, not bone-dry or soaking wet.

quests.instruction: Which word is the opposite of “accept”? (taking a gift with a smile vs. politely saying, “No, thank you.”)
quests.hint: What would you say to a second helping you don’t want?
quests.explanation: Accepting means saying yes to what’s offered. Declining means politely saying no.
quests.funFact: “Accept” and “except” sound alike but mean very different things.

quests.instruction: Maya turned off the tap while brushing her teeth, which saved water. Leaving it running all the time would ___ it.
quests.hint: Where does all that extra water go?
quests.explanation: Saving means using something carefully so there’s more left. Wasting means using it up for no good reason.
quests.funFact: A tap that drips steadily can lose thousands of litres in a year.

quests.instruction: In many places the days get shorter in winter. In spring, the hours of daylight…
quests.hint: Compare the evening light in December with the evening light in May.
quests.explanation: Increasing means getting bigger or more. Decreasing means getting smaller or less.
quests.funFact: In the north, the shortest day of the year is around December 21.

quests.instruction: Aiden practiced spelling every evening, so his scores got better each week. If he stopped practicing for months, they might…
quests.hint: Does a skill grow or fade when you stop using it?
quests.explanation: Getting better means improving. Getting worse means slipping backward.
quests.funFact: Practice strengthens the connections between brain cells.

quests.instruction: Lila says pizza is the best lunch. Her friend says, “No, I like pasta more.” The two of them…
quests.hint: Do the two friends share the same opinion?
quests.explanation: When people agree, they share the same opinion. When they disagree, their opinions differ.
quests.funFact: In many countries, people shake their heads sideways for “no”, but in a few, such as Bulgaria, the gestures are reversed.

quests.instruction: Which word is the opposite of “allow”? (a gate that lets everyone through vs. a gate that keeps everyone out)
quests.hint: Think of a rule that begins with “You must not…”.
quests.explanation: To allow is to say something is fine to do. To forbid is to say it must not be done.
quests.funFact: Many parks forbid feeding wild animals because our food can make them ill.

quests.instruction: The teacher said, “What lovely handwriting!” That was praise. Pointing out only what’s wrong in a harsh voice would be to…
quests.hint: Which word means finding fault?
quests.explanation: Praising shows you approve of something. Criticizing points out what you think is wrong.
quests.funFact: “Praise” comes from a Latin word for “price” or “value”.

quests.instruction: The magician pulled a coin from behind your ear, so it appeared. Then he covered it with a cloth and it…
quests.hint: What happened to the coin when the cloth lifted?
quests.explanation: To appear is to come into view. To disappear is to go out of view.
quests.funFact: Many magic tricks work because your eyes follow one hand while the trick happens somewhere else.

quests.instruction: Dev hid the birthday gift in his cupboard for a week. On the party day, he proudly…
quests.hint: A present has been hidden for a week. The party is the moment it comes out.
quests.explanation: To hide is to keep something out of sight. To show is to let people see it.
quests.funFact: Chameleons and stick insects survive by hiding in plain sight.

quests.instruction: Anya snapped the toy bricks together to build a tall tower. At tidy-up time, she had to…
quests.hint: What do you do to a tower before it can go back into the box?
quests.explanation: Snapping together joins pieces. Pulling them apart separates them again.
quests.funFact: Interlocking toy bricks from the 1950s still fit with ones made today.

quests.instruction: The alarm rings and Pia wakes up. After a long day, at bedtime, she…
quests.hint: What happens when she snuggles under the blanket and closes her eyes?
quests.explanation: Waking up means moving from sleep to being aware. Falling asleep is the reverse.
quests.funFact: Most children aged six to twelve need about nine to twelve hours of sleep.

quests.instruction: In the school play, the knights marched toward the cardboard castle. When the dragon puppet roared, they all…
quests.hint: When something startles you, your feet move before you decide.
quests.explanation: To advance is to move forward. To retreat is to move back, away from what’s ahead.
quests.funFact: In chess, a pawn can only move forward, never backward.

quests.instruction: Tara loves dogs and walks right up to every friendly one. Her brother is nervous, so he tends to…
quests.hint: Which way does he step when a dog trots near?
quests.explanation: To approach is to move closer to something. To avoid is to keep away from it.
quests.funFact: Dogs wag their tails for many reasons, not only when they’re happy.

quests.instruction: Everyone in the class got a part in the play, so no one was left out. It would be unfair to…
quests.hint: Which word means leaving someone out?
quests.explanation: Including means making sure someone is part of the group. Excluding means leaving them out.
quests.funFact: Some playgrounds are designed to be inclusive, so children of all abilities can play together.

quests.instruction: Kim tried the puzzle ten times. On the tenth try, she finally finished it. If the pieces had fallen apart again, she would have…
quests.hint: Think of an attempt that doesn’t work out.
quests.explanation: To succeed is to manage what you set out to do. To fail is to not manage it, at least this time.
quests.funFact: Thomas Edison tested many different materials before finding a light-bulb filament that lasted.

quests.instruction: The hikers climbed the mountain path for three hours. After lunch at the top, they began to…
quests.hint: Which way does the path lead after the summit?
quests.explanation: Climbing means going up. Descending means going down.
quests.funFact: Mount Everest is about 8,849 metres high.

quests.instruction: Dad lets the tub fill for a bath. When the bath is over, he pulls the plug so the water can…
quests.hint: Where does the water go once the plug is out?
quests.explanation: To fill is to make something full. To drain is to let the liquid run out until it’s gone.
quests.funFact: Bathtubs have an overflow hole near the top so water doesn’t spill over the sides.

quests.instruction: Which word is the opposite of “share”? (splitting a snack among the whole table vs. tucking it away in your bag for yourself)
quests.hint: Picture a snack that never leaves one person’s bag.
quests.explanation: To share is to let others have a part. To keep is to hold it all for yourself.
quests.funFact: “Share” is related to an old word meaning “to cut” or “to divide”.

quests.instruction: On school-trip day, Ila will bring her lunch from home. After lunch, she will ___ her empty box back with her.
quests.hint: Which word means carrying it away from the picnic spot?
quests.explanation: Bring means to carry something to a place. Take means to carry it away from there.
quests.funFact: In English, “come” and “bring” are about moving toward the speaker, while “go” and “take” are about moving away.

quests.instruction: At the door, the teacher says, “Please come in.” At home time, she says, “Now you may…”
quests.hint: Which way do you walk when the day is over?
quests.explanation: Come means moving toward where someone is. Go means moving away from it.
quests.funFact: “Come” and “go” are among the oldest words in English.

quests.instruction: Mira earns pocket money by watering a neighbor’s plants. At the toy shop, she…
quests.hint: Think about what changes when her coins cross the counter.
quests.explanation: To earn is to get money for work. To spend is to give it away in exchange for something.
quests.funFact: The word “piggy bank” comes from “pygg”, an old word for a kind of clay.

quests.instruction: Before the dive, Kiran’s shoulders were tense. After taking a deep breath, he let them…
quests.hint: What do your muscles do when you breathe out slowly?
quests.explanation: Tense muscles are tight and held hard. Relaxing lets them go loose and soft.
quests.funFact: Slow, deep breaths can help your body feel calmer.
